reason: A is more art-directed: one dominant Apple CTA, monochrome restraint, and specific hiking copy, with a true dark treatment. B is a competent form but blue icon and email CTA compete. Both clip at AX-XL; A hides email entirely, which keeps confidence medium.
A's buttons, contrast, and dark mode are fully resolved; B's secondary buttons look disabled and large text hides actions. B's copy and hierarchy are stronger, but execution favors A.

B is more restrained and stays usable at AX-XL, while A's giant CTA overlaps truncated product text and drops color/size controls. B also has richer, domain-specific content. B's description still collides with the fixed button, but A's large-text failure is decisive.

A is more disciplined: one accent, a clearer buy path, and a coherent dark treatment. B has useful commerce patterns but extra accents (mint stage, red badge, stars) and a bright hero in dark mode. Both overlap and clip at AX-XL.
B has one dominant figure, a single accent, native disclosure rows, and reflows at AX-XL. A is gradient card-soup with many icon colors; its hero amount splits and the ring collides at large text.

A wins on restraint and hierarchy: one orange accent, de-emphasized cents, and a clear eye path. B's gradient, multicolor icons, and ring add noise, and at AX-XL the ring collides with a currency amount that wraps mid-number. A's large-text layout clips secondary rows but stays readable.

B has one dominant spent total, monochrome rows, and a figure that stays intact at AX-XL. A’s balance competes with in/out stats and multicolor icons, and the amount splits across lines at large text.

B reflows at the largest text size while A's rows collide with the search field and clipped chips. B also reads as a complete banking list—balance, in/out, pending badges, chevrons—with a tuned dark mode. A is more restrained, but the broken accessibility layout is decisive.

B is more restrained and native: one accent, pill controls, and dark mode with real surface steps. A’s gradient hero and repeated purple feel decorative, and AX-XL clips the sample card into the button. B truncates at large text but stays readable.

B holds a clear mic-to-headline-to-CTA path and keeps the pitch and button intact at AX-XL. A is cleaner but clips the second feature and breaks large text: truncated title, lost headline, wrapped CTA.

A is the more complete paywall: selectable monthly/yearly plans, de-emphasized price units, one accent, and a designed dark mode. B is warmer but overuses orange, omits plan choice, and clips the headline into the button at large text. Both fail AX-XL; A's trial block is also clipped.

B presents a real plan choice, restore, and price typography, so it reads as a finished paywall. A is prettier at default size but never offers monthly versus yearly, and at AX-XL the headline collides with the button. B also clips its trial block, yet solves the brief.

A is a native grouped settings list: one accent, writing-specific options, type that reflows at AX-XL. B’s gradient upsell, multicolor icons, blank header, missing appearance, and clipped large text look unfinished.

B reads as native Settings: quiet hierarchy, one accent, consistent grouping, and AX-XL text that wraps without clipping. A’s gradient plan card and multicolor icons over-decorate a settings screen, and large type overflows the subscription card.

A’s light and dark screens have a clearer metric, stricter accent use, native grouped runs, and richer workout detail. B reflows at AX-XL instead of clipping the distance, but cards, icons, and a missing nav title feel more generic.

B reads as a native running screen: large title, specific workouts, and a quieter accent. A is polished but card-heavy, with a ring, pills, and icon tiles competing. Both break at AX-XL; B loses the hero number, yet its default hierarchy and realism still look more designed.
